newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- APRIL 16.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--High income earners have been paying progressively more taxes despite constituting a proportionally small number of taxpayers, according to a study conducted on taxation over the period 1992-1995 and printed in the Bank of Greece circular. Social insurance contributions in the public sector and banks however increased markedly, leading to less money in the hand and more claims for wage increases.

--Reports say the National Bank of Greece has seen an increase in net profits in the order of 30-40 percent in the first quarter, giving the bank's administration an optimistic outlook on the imminent share capital increase.
--The Bank of Piraeus is expected to finalise the terms of a majority stake in Sigma Securities within the next few days.

--The foreign ministry will contribute decisively to the promotion of Greek business plans in Eastern Europe and the Middle East, leading Greek entrepreneurs were told yesterday at a meeting with Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos.
--Greek diplomatic services abroad will be directed to afford more assistance to Greek businesses, Pangalos said, stressing the emphasis the country places on economic diplomacy.

--The OECD has sounded the alarm bell for Greece's course towards Maastricht, saying deficits and unemployment will fail to meet targets. The divergence in figures in the the first quarter, OECD says, indicates a trend that will be difficult to reverse.

--The stock market will see changes to the brokerage scene, with the creation of stronger and bigger brokerage firms operating under the umbrella of banking groups. Alpha Trust will discuss the issue of merging with a securities firm at its general assembly next Tuesday.

--Computer cross-checking has revealed three million taxpayers with more than one tax file number. The scam was revealed by the new computerised taxation programme TAXIS, which has begun to be applied at the finance ministry.
--Forex lending constituted a third of total bank lending to business and consumers last year, up from only a quarter in 1995, according to the Bank of Greece.

--The reduction of charges and tariffs to trade between Greece and Turkey will be to the advantage of Greece's food and consumer items markets. The guidelines are expected to get the green light on April 29 at the EU-Turkey Association Council.

--The dollar and pound sterling hit new highs against the drachma on money markets yesterday. The dollar has risen 10.33 percent since the beginning of the year and the pound 5.66 percent. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
